title: 边开会边写文档：怎样让讨论留下清楚结论
topic: 边开会边写文档：怎样让讨论留下清楚结论

source.title: GitLab Meeting Best Practices: Live Doc Meetings | The GitLab Handbook
source.license: 原文按项目方确认的授权收录

paragraphs: On this page, we’re detailing how to create efficient, transparent, documentation-based meetings leveraging GitLab’s proven principles. This style of meeting increases cohesion, discipline, and transparency regardless of the work environment.

“No agenda, no attenda.” Every work-related meeting should have a live doc agenda affixed to the calendar invite. To better understand how GitLab utilizes agenda docs, here’s a templated example you can copy and use in your organization. Coffee chats are excluded from this given their function in informal communication.
If you determine that a meeting is needed to move a project forward, address a blocker, or resolve a miscommunication, follow the proven principles below.

Create the agenda in a Google Doc ahead of time using GitLab’s Agenda Template (this can be any shared document service, though GitLab uses Google Workspace). Please do not use Google Calendar’s automatic agenda/notes creation function, as it does not adhere to GitLab’s preferred agenda flow. If the automatic agenda doc has been created in error, edit the calendar invite and hover over the X to delete it from the agenda to avoid confusion.
Ensure that the appropriate sharing settings are in place to prevent a chorus of “I can’t access the agenda” comments; agendas should be editable by all participants.
translations: 在本页中，我们将详细介绍如何利用 GitLab 经过验证的原则，创建高效、透明的基于文档的会议。这种会议方式无论工作环境如何，都能增强凝聚力、纪律性和透明度。
“无议程，不参会。”每个与工作相关的会议都应在日历邀请中附加实时文档议程。为了更好地了解 GitLab 如何使用议程文档，这里有一个可复制并在贵组织中使用的模板示例。咖啡聊天因其非正式沟通功能而被排除在外。
如果您确定需要召开会议以推进项目、解决障碍或消除误解，请遵循以下经过验证的原则。
请提前使用 GitLab 的议程模板在 Google 文档中创建议程（这可以是任何共享文档服务，尽管 GitLab 使用 Google Workspace）。请不要使用 Google 日历的自动议程/笔记创建功能，因为它不符合 GitLab 首选的议程流程。如果错误地创建了自动议程文档，请编辑日历邀请并将鼠标悬停在 X 上以将其从议程中删除，以免造成混淆。
确保设置了适当的共享设置，以避免出现“我无法访问议程"的集体评论；议程应允许所有参与者编辑。
fullTextParagraphs: On this page, we’re detailing how to create efficient, transparent, documentation-based meetings leveraging GitLab’s proven principles. This style of meeting increases cohesion, discipline, and transparency regardless of the work environment.

“No agenda, no attenda.” Every work-related meeting should have a live doc agenda affixed to the calendar invite. To better understand how GitLab utilizes agenda docs, here’s a templated example you can copy and use in your organization. Coffee chats are excluded from this given their function in informal communication.
If you determine that a meeting is needed to move a project forward, address a blocker, or resolve a miscommunication, follow the proven principles below.

Create the agenda in a Google Doc ahead of time using GitLab’s Agenda Template (this can be any shared document service, though GitLab uses Google Workspace). Please do not use Google Calendar’s automatic agenda/notes creation function, as it does not adhere to GitLab’s preferred agenda flow. If the automatic agenda doc has been created in error, edit the calendar invite and hover over the X to delete it from the agenda to avoid confusion.
Ensure that the appropriate sharing settings are in place to prevent a chorus of “I can’t access the agenda” comments; agendas should be editable by all participants.
Link the agenda in the meeting invite.
Establish the agenda as far in advance of the meeting as possible.
Agendas should use numbered lists, not bulleted lists.
Context section includes: The goal(s) of the meeting; clear pre-work or pre-watch/read instructions; intent and expected outcomes using low-context communication.
Pre-read/watch or pre-work materials should be emailed to attendees at least 24 hours in advance.
The meeting host (DRI) may summarize key points and context for the first 1 to 2 minutes of the meeting, but few meetings should be presentations.
Questions should be written and listed in advance of the scheduled meeting time; this tends to increase the quality of questions.
Make a proposal whenever feasible. It should be possible to answer/comment with a simple “yes.”
Link any relevant piece of text to associated resources to prevent people from spending time searching or asking.

Follow GitLab’s smart note taking guidance by taking notes inline with the agenda rather than using a separate “notes” section. Real-time note-taking by multiple participants is encouraged. Another good reference is the CEO Shadow handbook page tips section, specifically It's helpful if shadow one takes notes as the first speaker is talking, then shadow two starts when the next speaker continues the conversation. Shadow one can pick up note taking again when the next speaker contributes. By alternating this way, the shadows are better able to keep up with all the participants in the conversation. This advice can be used in general meetings as well.

Another good reference is the CEO Shadow handbook page tips section, specifically It's helpful if shadow one takes notes as the first speaker is talking, then shadow two starts when the next speaker continues the conversation. Shadow one can pick up note taking again when the next speaker contributes. By alternating this way, the shadows are better able to keep up with all the participants in the conversation. This advice can be used in general meetings as well.

If you’re not talking in the meeting, at any given time, help take notes. If there isn’t a note taker listed in the document at the start of the meeting, people should self-note-take. Consider asking other people to write down the answers in real-time to allow the person who asked the question to focus on the answer. The person asking the question can touch up the answer when the conversation has moved on to something less relevant to them.
Notes should be properly indented and structured to follow the conversation’s flow.
Notes do not have to be verbatim, but they should capture key points made and be clear on any decisions or next steps.
Preface questions and answers with the participant’s name, giving context to the origin.
Follow the order of the questions instead of jumping around in the agenda; this prevents the proverbial loudest voice in the room from dominating a conversation.
Always ask if the name preceding the question would like to verbalize; if they wish not to, or are otherwise unavailable, the meeting host should verbalize on their behalf.

Reenact questions in the list by verbalizing them even if they were already asked and answered in the shared document. Hearing the question and answer allows everyone to think about it and respond to it. It might also happen that when verbalizing the question or answer more context is given since most people can talk faster and with less effort than they can type. Another advantage if you’re recording the meeting is that the recording contains everything.
Unless the meeting contains Not Public information, record the meeting to share with those who cannot attend live and consider livestreaming for maximum transparency and feedback potential.
If a portion of a meeting does not pertain to you, it’s OK to look away. You are the manager of your own time and attention.

Establishing a culture where team members are cognizant that they work with others who may be in a different location, or unable to attend a meeting live, is critical. Documentation is a vital part of avoiding team dysfunction.

Improving your meeting hygiene can start by shifting to live doc meetings. It is a relatively simple step, and tends to create an understanding of the value of documentation. If you’re looking for a place to start in capturing team-wide buy-in on documentation, consider adding agendas to all work-related meetings and insist on live documentation during them.

It prevents knowledge leaks. Meetings without agendas are only useful to those in it, and even then, it’s likely that outcomes will be forgotten, or critical pieces of the puzzle will become less familiar over time.

It creates a more inclusive meeting atmosphere. People can add questions and insights before (and even after) a synchronous meeting. Plus, those who are less comfortable verbalizing points in front of management can use the agenda doc to properly articulate their complete thoughts.

It creates a takeaway. The agenda doc lives longer after the meeting. If you want to share it further, perhaps sending to a person or team that you realize would have benefited from attending, you’re able to do so.

It shifts the memorization burden away from humans. If there’s an agenda doc affixed to each calendar invite, you can easily search your calendar for key words (marketing, CEO, engineering, etc.), find a given meeting, and immediately access a documented history of what was discussed.

Not all meetings are inherently bad. We encourage managers to establish regular 1:1 meetings with their team, for example. There are instances where a brief synchronous chat can replace multiple hours of asynchronous work. Strategically leveraging sync and async is an art, not a science.
Many meetings can be avoided by understanding how to work well asynchronously.
For a deeper dive on how GitLab implements meetings in a remote work environment, visit our all-remote meetings guide. To learn more about how GitLab communications, visit our Communications page.

A live doc meeting is a GitLab specialty. It’s a work-related meeting (e.g. not a coffee chat) where you document everything live (yes, everything)! Start documenting before the meetings begins by attaching a shared, editable agenda document to the calendar invite.

Here is a sample template for a live doc meeting. Be sure to create a new Google Doc and attach a link to your live doc with every calendar invite. Please do not use Google Calendar’s automatic agenda/notes creation function, as it does not adhere to GitLab’s preferred agenda flow. Include the agenda for the meeting, set the appropriate sharing permissions, and add instructions for expected engagement (in Context section) so team members understand how to contribute whether they attend synchronously or asynchronously.
A live document is a document that may continually be edited and updated. Examples could include a shared Google doc, whiteboard being used by a team for collaboration, or GitLab’s handbook.

There are two ways to participate in a live doc meeting: either synchronously, like when joining a live Zoom call, or asynchronously, by reviewing the documented discussion along with any recorded video after the meeting is over.

Live doc meetings are usually held in the host’s time zone. However, leaders should rotate meetings to accommodate a more diverse array of time zones as well as record them so that others can watch at a later time.

Live doc meetings can happen fully in-person, fully online, or a on hybrid call — which is a blend of both. It’s best to have everyone on a level playing field for communication and discussion, so hybrid calls should be avoided. If a hybrid call is necessary, have participants use their own equipment (camera, headset, screen) to avoid audio problems from delays and feedback.
Return to the main all-remote page.

notes.explain: 指会议过程和结果都通过文档记录和管理的会议方式，强调透明度和可追溯性
notes.example: Our team has adopted documentation-based meetings to ensure all decisions are properly recorded and accessible.

notes.explain: 会议管理原则，强调议程对于会议的必要性，没有议程的会议不值得参加
notes.example: As our company policy states, 'No agenda, no attenda' is strictly enforced for all project meetings.

notes.meaning: 自动议程/笔记创建功能
notes.explain: 日历软件自动生成会议议程的功能，但GitLab不推荐使用，因为不符合其议程流程
notes.example: Please disable the automatic agenda/notes creation function in our calendar system to maintain consistency.

notes.explain: 确保文档能被所有会议参与者访问和编辑的权限配置
notes.example: Before the meeting, double-check the appropriate sharing settings for the project documentation.

scenario.title: Keeping meeting decisions in a shared live document
english: The team needs a meeting document that everyone can edit during the discussion.
A shared agenda can capture the questions, decisions, and follow-up as the meeting happens.
You suggest using one live document instead of separate automatic notes.
chinese: 团队需要一份能在讨论过程中共同编辑的会议文档。
共享议程可以边开会边记录问题、决定和后续安排。
你建议用一份实时协作文档，代替分散的自动会议记录。

firstAttempt.prompt: 团队在讨论中决定保持当前发布日期、缩小首批试点范围，并由 Maya 周四前确认周末客服覆盖。请用英文同步决定、单独列出仍待确认的问题，并写明负责人和期限。
firstAttempt.sample: Decision: We’ll keep the current launch date and reduce the first rollout group. Open question: Can Support cover the weekend launch? Maya will confirm coverage with Support by Thursday.
firstAttempt.rationale: 讨论过程中记录决定、待确认问题和负责人，避免结论散落在会后记忆里。

words.example: A shared live document makes the discussion and decisions visible to everyone.
words.translation: 共享实时文档让所有人都能看到讨论和决定。
words.note: 在职场环境中，透明度通常指信息共享的开放程度，是高效协作的基础

words.example: Recording decisions in one place helps maintain cohesion across teams working in different time zones.
words.translation: 把决定记录在同一处，有助于不同时区的团队保持协同。
words.note: 指群体成员之间的凝聚力。

words.example: Add any blocker to the live document so the team can discuss it.
words.translation: 把阻碍记入实时文档，方便团队讨论。
words.note: 在敏捷开发中，blocker指阻碍项目进展的问题或障碍

words.example: The meeting notes were affixed to the project brief so new teammates could find the decision history.
words.translation: 会议记录附在项目简报后，方便新加入的同事查阅决策过程。
words.note: affix 是较正式的“附上”，常见于通知、表格或标签。

words.example: All employees must adhere to the company's data security guidelines when working remotely.
words.translation: 所有员工在远程工作时都必须遵守公司的数据安全准则。
words.note: 指遵守规则、标准或双方约定。

words.example: The manager was met with a chorus of complaints about the new work policy.
words.translation: 经理收到了对新工作政策的齐声抱怨。
words.note: a chorus of complaints 常形容多人接连表达不满。

structure.original: On this page, we’re detailing how to create efficient, transparent, documentation-based meetings leveraging GitLab’s proven principles.
analysis: “On this page”交代页面范围；主句“we’re detailing”使用现在进行时。
“how to create…”是 how 引导的疑问词不定式结构，作 detailing 的宾语；efficient、transparent、documentation-based 并列修饰 meetings。
“leveraging GitLab’s proven principles”补充说明这些会议所依据的原则；leveraging 是现在分词形式。
structure.transfer: We’ll record decisions, owners, due dates, and open questions in one live document as the meeting happens.

rewrite.bad: I’ll send my notes after the meeting. The rest of the team can ask if they need details.
rewrite.good: Decision: We’ll keep the current launch date and reduce the first rollout group. Open question: Can Support cover the weekend launch? Maya will confirm with Support by Thursday.
rewrite.translation: 决定：保持当前发布日期，并缩小首批试点范围。待确认：客服能否覆盖周末上线？Maya 会在周四前向客服团队确认。
rewrite.pattern: Decision: [agreed action]. Open question: [unresolved issue]? [Owner] will confirm [next step] by [date].

cloze.prompt: ___: keep the current launch date and reduce the first rollout group.
cloze.why: 边讨论边写结论，让参与者及时校对理解。

cloze.prompt: ___ question: Can Support cover the weekend launch?
cloze.why: 明确区分定论与未决事项。

cloze.prompt: ___ will confirm weekend coverage with Support by Thursday.
cloze.why: 把结论落到负责人和截止时间。

dictation.text: Sarah, a project coordinator, needs to finalize the quarterly report while attending a team meeting about budget allocations.
She struggles to keep up with the discussion while documenting key points, missing critical decisions that affect her report.

translationPractice.prompt: 决定：保持当前发布日期，并缩小首批上线范围。
translationPractice.answer: Decision: keep the current launch date and reduce the first rollout group.

translationPractice.prompt: 待确认：客服团队能否支持周末上线？
translationPractice.answer: Open question: Can Support cover the weekend launch?

translationPractice.prompt: 我们安排 Maya 在周四前向客服团队确认周末支持安排。
translationPractice.answer: Let’s assign Maya to confirm weekend coverage with Support by Thursday.

choice.prompt: 产品上线讨论中，团队已决定保持发布日期，但客服是否能覆盖周末仍待确认。请选出能记录决定、待确认问题、负责人和期限的表达。
options: Let’s use the calendar’s auto-notes. Only the meeting host needs to edit them, and decisions can be added later.
Decision: We’ll keep the current launch date and reduce the first rollout group. Open question: Can Support cover the weekend launch? Maya will confirm coverage with Support by Thursday.
Let’s each keep private notes and compare them after the meeting.
choice.why: 把已确定的决定、未解决的问题和负责确认的人及期限分开写清楚。

output.prompt: 在讨论客服排班时，团队决定先试行两周晚间轮值，由 Nina 周五前确认人员安排；周末是否延长覆盖仍未决定。请用英文记录决定、待确认问题、负责人和期限。
output.sample: Decision: We’ll pilot evening coverage for two weeks. Open question: Will weekend coverage also be extended? Nina will confirm the staffing plan by Friday.
check: 是否把已作决定和待确认问题分开？
是否写明负责人和截止时间？
是否让讨论中的决定留在共享文档里？

blockers: 听写讲一边开会一边赶季度报告，与本期共享文档记录讨论结论的主题不符；需同步修复音频与文本。
